newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Police prepare to wreck shacks at Jewish settlement.
newsitem.headline: Police prepare to wreck shacks at Jewish settlement.

text.p: Israeli police brought a bulldozer to a Jewish settlement in the West Bank on Tuesday to wreck three shacks built illegally, officials and witnesses said.

A police spokeswoman said 200 troops went to the settlement of Yitzhar near the Palestinian town of Nablus to demolish the wooden structures and prevent violence. She said the shacks were erected several months ago.
But a settler leader said the shacks were built two years ago 300 metres (yards) from the settlement and were homes to members of the community.
"It was imperative for our security to build homes on this hill. How strange it is that this government suddenly finds it necessary to wreck them," Yitzhar resident Yehuda Lievemen told Reuters.
He said settler leaders were trying to convince police not to demolish the homes.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government has approved the expansion of several settlements in the West Bank despite Palestinian protests but last week police carted away three mobile homes settlers placed on a West Bank hill in a bid to enlarge their community.
Israel's groundbreaking for a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March plunged peacemaking with the Arabs into crisis.
